message.content: **What I did and why:** I reviewed the saved notes (long-term holder, dividends reinvested manually) and the account (100,000 USD cash, 20 AMZN shares, no GOOGL position), then checked the GOOGL quote at 171.12 last / 171.10 bid / 171.14 ask as of 2024-11-06 15:05 UTC. GOOGL is within the permitted universe, and the fundamentals from its FY2023 10-K (filed 2024-01-31) support adding a long-term position: revenue of $307,394M, net income of $73,795M, diluted EPS of $5.80, and operating cash flow of $101,746M — a highly cash-generative business trading at roughly 29.5x trailing EPS. I therefore placed a single buy limit order for 140 shares at $171.50, a limit about 0.2% above the current market price (well within "close to market"), which filled at $171.50 for a total of $24,010 — under the $25,000 per-order cap and, as the only trade today, under the $50,000 daily cap, with no money moved out of the account (remaining cash ≈ $75,990). No further orders were placed.
